newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE CLOSE IN AS TOP TWO DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE CLOSE IN AS TOP TWO DRAW.

text.p: Another brilliant goal by England midfielder David Beckham earned Manchester United a point from a 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge on Saturday after Gianfranco Zola had put Chelsea ahead.

United stayed top of the English league standings as Liverpool could only draw 0-0 at home to Blackburn despite dominating throughout. Newcastle moved into third as a Les Ferdinand goal was enough to win 1-0 at bottom club Middlesbrough.
Ian Marshall scored a hat-trick in the first 27 minutes to help Leicester beat Derby 4-2 while Sheffield Wednesday came from two down to win 3-2 at Southampton.
Leeds won 1-0 at Sunderland and Coventry against Everton and Nottingham Forest against Aston Villa ended goalless.
The results kept Manchester United top on 54 points, one ahead of Liverpool. Newcastle have 48 with a game in hand, ahead on goal difference of Arsenal, who play Wimbledon on Sunday.
Zola waltzed through a static United defence to put Chelsea ahead after just two minutes.
Mark Hughes should have made it 2-0 soon afterwards but fluffed his shot -- and Chelsea never wnet as close again.
United hauled themselves back into the game and claimed a fully deserved point when Beckham seized on a poor header by Trevor Sinclair to crash a superb volley into the roof of the net.
Blackburn's first win of the season came against Liverpool back in November when the Ewood Park club were still rooted to the foot of the table.
They continued their climb away from the danger zone -- but Liverpool will be wondering just how they failed to win.
The usually deadly Robbie Fowler proved strangely out of touch as he squandered four chances he would normally have tucked away with ease.
Two of his efforts hit the woodwork after neat passing moves had opened up the Blackburn defence -- the other two disappeared high into the stand.
Jason McAteer and Steve McManaman also missed good opportunites and Dominic Matteo thumped a header agains the bar in the last minute.
"It was a game of missed chances," said McAteer. "We created plenty but just couldn't seem to finish them."
Liverpool's home form has been their weakness this season with a defeat and now six draws at the usually impregnable Anfield.
McAteer recognized the problem. "We need to find more consistancy and win a few more at home," said the Ireland international. "The dressing room was dead after today."
Another changing room to be avoided was the one marked "Home" at the Dell after Southampton threw away a 2-0 halftime lead.
Egil Ostenstad and Matt Le Tissier from the penalty spot had Southampton looking good but two goals in six minutes by David Hirst levelled things and Andy Booth hit the winner 12 minutes from time.
"We knew we could play much better," said Hirst. "In the second half we threw caution to the wind."
Wednesday have now lost only once in their last 20 games while Southampton looked ever more likely relegation-bound.
Middlesbrough, expected to join them, were somewhat unlucky to lose to local rivals Newcastle.
Les Ferdinand shot Newcastle ahead in the eighth minute but Bryan Robson's side looked the more dangerous from then on.
Clayton Blackmore hit a post for Boro and then Fabrizio Ravanelli thought he had scored only for the goal to be ruled out for a foul.
Derby went ahead through Dean Sturridge after two minutes at Leicester -- only to fall 3-1 behind 25 minutes later as Marshall thumped in a 25-yarder and followed with two tap-ins.
Sturridge hit a second before Steve Claridge settled it for Leicester.
Lee Bowyer kept up his good recent scoring run to give Leeds the points at Sunderland but the return of Dion Dublin after a seven-game ban did not help Coventry to find the net against Everton.
Wayward finishing was the main ingredient at Nottingham Forest where Villa missed several decent opportunities.
